sections.title: Grade 1 foundations
sections.description: Words, sentences and writing basics from Grade 1 that every Grade 3 learner needs.

questions.question: Which day comes just before Saturday?
questions.options: Friday | Thursday | Monday | Sunday
questions.explanation: In the week, Friday comes first and then Saturday follows it.

questions.question: Who is the helper who puts out fires?
questions.options: A reporter | A window cleaner | A bus driver | A firefighter
questions.explanation: A firefighter is the brave helper who puts out fires and keeps people safe.

questions.question: We use a ruler to ___ how long something is.
questions.options: pour | sing | taste | measure
questions.explanation: A ruler helps us measure length — how long or short something is.

questions.question: Which room has a sink and is used for cooking food?
questions.options: The bathroom | The kitchen | The bedroom | The living room
questions.explanation: The kitchen is the room where food is cooked and the dishes are washed.

questions.question: Where do you go to post a letter?
questions.options: The post office | The swimming pool | The playground | The bakery
questions.explanation: The post office is the place in the city where we post letters and parcels.

questions.question: Read the sentence: 'My neighbour is a doctor. She helps people who are ___.' Which word fits the gap?
questions.options: sick | empty | loud | green
questions.explanation: A doctor helps people who are sick, so 'sick' is the word that fits.

questions.question: Read the two sentences: 'The sun shines in the day. The moon shines at night.' When does the moon shine?
questions.options: In the morning | At night | At noon | In the day
questions.explanation: The sentence tells us the moon shines at night — good reading detective work!

questions.question: Read the clue: 'This small creature has eight legs and spins a web.' What is it?
questions.options: A spider | A bee | An ant | A butterfly
questions.explanation: A spider has eight legs and spins a sticky web to catch its food.

questions.question: In the text 'Different Kinds of Homes', Leo says his home is a flat on the fifth floor. What is a flat?
questions.options: A set of rooms inside a bigger building | A small house made of mud | A house built on tall wooden legs | A tent for camping
questions.correctAnswer: A set of rooms inside a bigger building
questions.explanation: Leo explains that a flat is a set of rooms that is part of a bigger building — that is why he rides the lift to the fifth floor.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.options: She is likes mangoes. | She like mangoes. | She liking mangoes. | She likes mangoes.
questions.explanation: With he or she we add -s to the verb, and we do not put 'is' before it: 'She likes mangoes.'

questions.question: Which question asks about a birthday correctly?
questions.options: When is your birthday? | Your birthday when is? | Is when your birthday? | When your birthday is?
questions.explanation: A question starts with the question word, then the verb: 'When is your birthday?'

questions.question: Which sentence compares two animals correctly?
questions.options: A giraffe is taller a horse. | A giraffe is taller than a horse. | A giraffe is more tall than a horse. | A giraffe is tall than a horse.
questions.correctAnswer: A giraffe is taller than a horse.
questions.explanation: To compare two things we add -er to a short describing word and use 'than': taller than.

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'There are' correctly?
questions.options: There is two beds in the room. | There are is two beds in the room. | There are a bed in the room. | There are two beds in the room.
questions.correctAnswer: There are two beds in the room.
questions.explanation: We say 'There is' for one thing and 'There are' for more than one — two beds needs 'There are'.

questions.question: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.options: my name is amal | My name is Amal | My Name Is Amal. | My name is Amal.
questions.explanation: A sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, and a person's name always starts with a capital letter too.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly joins the two ideas with 'because'?
questions.options: I like reading because it is fun. | I like reading it is fun because. | Because I like reading fun it is. | I like reading it because is fun.
questions.correctAnswer: I like reading because it is fun.
questions.explanation: The word 'because' joins a sentence to its reason, and the reason comes straight after it.

questions.question: Which sentence is an instruction, telling someone what to do?
questions.options: Sweep the floor, please. | The floor is clean. | Did you sweep the floor? | The broom is old.
questions.explanation: An instruction tells somebody to do something, so it is a command like 'Sweep the floor, please.'

questions.question: Which word correctly joins these directions: 'Go straight, ___ turn left at the corner.'?
questions.options: then | is | red | swim
questions.explanation: 'Then' shows what to do next, so it links the two steps of the direction in the right order.

questions.question: Your mother's mother is your ___.
questions.options: sister | teacher | grandmother | friend
questions.explanation: Your mother's mother is your grandmother — a special member of your family.

questions.question: Which vehicle has spinning blades on top and can land on grass?
questions.options: A train | A bicycle | A helicopter | A boat
questions.explanation: A helicopter has spinning blades on top and can land almost anywhere, even on grass.

questions.question: In the story 'Breakfast at Grandma's House', how many grapes did Amal count on the table?
questions.options: Five | Ten | Four | One
questions.explanation: In the story, Amal counted ten grapes on Grandma's table, one by one all the way to ten.

questions.question: In the story 'Breakfast at Grandma's House', what job did Grandma ask Amal to do?
questions.options: Cook the breakfast | Lay the table | Wash the dishes | Carry the baby
questions.explanation: Grandma asked Amal to lay the table, and Amal happily put out the little bowls.

questions.question: Read the sentence: 'Rain falls from the ___.' Which word fits the gap?
questions.options: table | sky | shoe | ground
questions.explanation: Rain falls down from the clouds in the sky onto the ground.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the correct order?
questions.options: Can a see I cat. | I can see a cat. | See can I a cat. | A cat I see can.
questions.explanation: English sentences follow an order: who, then the doing words — 'I can see a cat.'

questions.question: Which sentence talks about a girl in the family correctly?
questions.options: He is my sister. | She is my sister. | She my sister is. | Is she my sister she.
questions.explanation: We use 'she' for a girl or a woman, so a sister needs 'she is my sister.'

questions.question: Which sentence uses 'an' correctly?
questions.options: I can see an bus. | I can see a aeroplane. | I can see an aeroplane. | I can see an car.
questions.explanation: We use 'an' before a word that starts with an a, e, i, o or u sound, like 'aeroplane.'

questions.question: Which sentence uses a capital letter correctly?
questions.options: i see a cat. | I see a cat. | I See A Cat. | I see A cat.
questions.explanation: The word 'I' is always written with a capital letter, and a sentence starts with just one capital letter, right at the beginning.

questions.question: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.options: this is my sister amal | This is my sister, Amal. | This Is My Sister Amal | this is my sister, amal.
questions.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter, and a person's name — like Amal — always starts with a capital letter too.

questions.question: Which word correctly joins these steps: 'First we wait, ___ we get on the bus.'?
questions.options: then | is | red | cat
questions.explanation: 'Then' shows what happens next, joining the two steps of the journey in the right order.
